paper_metadata.title: Multiplicative-Weights Methods and Gibbs-State Preparation for Conic Portfolio Optimization: A Mathematical Framework Connecting Quantum Algorithms, Jordan Algebras, and Quantitative Finance
paper_metadata.venue: Artificial Intelligence Finance Institute (AIFI) working paper / preprint, January 20, 2026

summary: Theoretical framework bridging conic portfolio optimization (LP/SOCP/SDP formulations of mean-variance, risk-budgeting, CVaR, Sharpe, robust) to quantum multiplicative-weights (MW) feasibility solvers via Gibbs-state preparation over Jordan-algebraic SOCP arrowhead structure. Key contributions: complete SOCP-representability proofs; rigorous arrowhead spectral decomposition with rank-2 Gibbs objects; explicit MW complexity bounds; SDP relaxation pathway for cardinality-constrained portfolios. Headline iteration-complexity comparison (Table 1) for SOCP solving: classical IPM O(sqrt(r) log(1/eps)) iterations at O(r^3) per iteration (high precision ~1e-8); classical MW O(R^2/eps^2) iterations at O(r) per iteration (moderate ~1e-3); quantum MW O(sqrt(r)/eps^2) iterations (moderate). MW feasibility requires T = O(R^2 log(d)/eps^2) iterations in the symmetric-cone formulation. No numerical experiment, simulation, or hardware run; the paper identifies end-to-end benchmarks as open future work.

experiments.description: Theoretical complexity analysis of multiplicative-weights (MW) SOCP feasibility solvers for conic portfolio optimization. Compares classical interior-point methods (IPM), classical MW, and quantum MW (using Gibbs-state preparation over the SOCP arrowhead structure) on the iteration count and per-iteration cost required to solve SOCP feasibility problems arising from mean-variance, Sharpe-ratio, CVaR, and robust portfolio formulations. No simulation; bounds are analytical.

algorithm.variant: Quantum multiplicative-weights (MW) SOCP feasibility solver using Gibbs-state preparation over the SOCP arrowhead matrix representation of the Lorentz cone (rank-2 Jordan-algebraic structure); paired with classical IPM and classical MW baselines
algorithm.optimizer: Multiplicative-Weights update (Matrix MW) with learning rate eta = Theta(sqrt(log N / (R^2 T)))

hyperparameters.iterations_T: T = O(R^2 log d / eps^2) for MW feasibility

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Core portfolio problems reduced to LP/SOCP/SDP feasibility: (i) Markowitz mean-variance as SOCP; (ii) Sharpe-ratio maximization as quasi-convex reducible to SOCP via bisection with O(log(U/eps)) subproblems; (iii) CVaR minimization as LP; (iv) robust mean-variance as SOCP; (v) cardinality-constrained mean-variance via SDP lifting W = w w^T, W >= w w^T, continuous relaxation z_i in [0,1]. Quantum MW uses block-encoded Gibbs states exp(-beta H) with arrowhead structure giving rank-2 decompositions.
problem_formulation.constraints: budget 1^T w = 1; return target mu^T w >= rho; box/sector/turnover/leverage; risk-budgeting; cardinality sum z_i <= k; ellipsoidal or polyhedral uncertainty for robust

dataset_specification.description: Portfolio w in R^n with budget 1^T w = 1, return target mu^T w >= rho, covariance Sigma ≻ 0. Four worked formulations: mean-variance (SOCP), Sharpe-ratio (quasi-convex -> SOCP), CVaR (LP), robust mean-variance (SOCP). Cardinality-constrained extension via SDP lifting. Parameters n (assets), N_s (scenarios for CVaR), r (SOCP cone rank), d (ambient dimension), R (MW radius bound), eps (target accuracy) are symbolic.

results.notes: Table 1 (Section 10.3): Quantum MW O(sqrt(r)/eps^2) iterations for SOCP feasibility at moderate precision (~1e-3).
Section 5.x: MW feasibility on symmetric cones converges to eps-approx solution in T = O(R^2 log(d)/eps^2) iterations.
Section 3.x: maximizing Sharpe ratio reduces to O(log(U/eps)) SOCP feasibility subproblems via bisection on the quasi-convex level sets.
Section 5.4: Gibbs states for SOCP arrowhead matrices decompose as rank-2 objects (v_+ v_+^T + low-temperature correction), enabling efficient block-encoded preparation.
Proposition 10.1(b): asymptotic formula rho ~ v_+ v_+^T used when beta * r > 20 for numerical stability.

classical_baselines.notes: Table 1: O(sqrt(r) log(1/eps)) iterations; per-iteration cost O(r^3); achieves high precision (~1e-8).
Table 1: O(R^2/eps^2) iterations; per-iteration cost O(r) with SOCP structure; moderate precision (~1e-3).

speedup_claims.magnitude: Quantum MW iteration count O(sqrt(r)/eps^2) vs classical MW O(R^2/eps^2): sqrt improvement in cone rank / problem-dependent R factor; not a speedup over high-precision IPM when epsilon is small.
speedup_claims.notes: Advantage is in regimes where moderate precision suffices and r is large. Paper is explicit that precision/conditioning/data-access caveats may erode end-to-end advantage for realistic finance workloads.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Quantum MW: O(sqrt(r)/eps^2) SOCP MW iterations; MW feasibility T = O(R^2 log(d)/eps^2); Gibbs preparation via block-encoded polynomial approximation of exp(-beta H) with arrowhead rank-2 structure.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: IPM: O(sqrt(r) log(1/eps)) iterations at O(r^3) per iteration; classical MW: O(R^2/eps^2) iterations at O(r) per iteration.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Fault-tolerant block-encoded QRAM-style access to Sigma and r_i; fault-tolerant Gibbs-state preparation over arrowhead matrices; no explicit qubit/gate-count estimate given.
